title: Heaps and Priority Queues
summary: Keep the smallest or largest item instantly available while items keep arriving.
lesson:
How it works
- A binary heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array; every parent is no larger than its children in a min-heap.
- The children of index `i` are at `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`; its parent is at `(i - 1) / 2`.
- Insert appends and sifts up; remove-min swaps the last element to the root and sifts down. Both are `O(log n)`; peeking is `O(1)`.

When to reach for it
- You repeatedly need the minimum or maximum of a changing collection.
- The question asks for the top `k`, the `k`th largest, or the next event in time order.
- You are merging several sorted sources.

Common patterns
- Top `k`: keep a heap of size `k` and evict the worst whenever it grows larger.
- Scheduling: order pending work by time or priority and always take the earliest.
- In Java, `PriorityQueue` is a min-heap; pass `Comparator.reverseOrder()` for a max-heap.

Pitfalls
- Off-by-one index arithmetic in a hand-written heap.
- Forgetting to sift after replacing the root.
- Iterating a `PriorityQueue` does not visit elements in sorted order.
- Building by repeated insertion is `O(n log n)`; heapifying an array bottom-up is `O(n)`.
